Similar regressions employing real output have also been used to investigate the connection between real economic activity and money. In an important contribution, Sims (1972) introduced the notion of Granger causality into the debate over the real e¤ects of money. A variable X is said to Granger-cause Y if and only if lagged values of X have marginal predictive content in a forecasting equation for Y.
